Priya / team — technical plan and key knobs below. Long version in the loadplan attachment (loadplan.jmx).

Overview of runs:
- Baseline single-instance microbench to measure per-token processing and KV-cache hit latencies.
- Steady-state ramp: bring cluster to target concurrency (1k) over 10 minutes, hold 30 minutes, then step down.
- Burst test: short bursts to 2.5k concurrent for 2-5 minutes to evaluate queueing and backpressure behavior.
- End-to-end TTFT run with warmed prefix cache and cold-start scenarios.

Queueing/Rate-limit rules we will evaluate:
- Token-accept window: how many inflight requests are queued per GPU before shedding.
- Soft queueing thresholds (warn at 75% GPU load) vs hard limits (reject at 95%).
- Per-token throughput smoothing (burst token cap) to prevent large downstream latency spikes.

Tuning knobs to record and adjust:
- Batch size cap and dynamic batching latency floor.
- KV cache TTLs and prefix caching thresholds.
- Rate-limit config: per-route QPS, per-key concurrency caps, and global throttles with token backpressure.

We will produce a CSV of raw metrics (perf-results-20260412.csv) and an action list of recommended config changes. Attaching loadplan.jmx and sample Grafana dashboards.

Attachment: loadplan.jmx (JMeter plan)

- Will Redwood insert synthetic variance (jitter) into inter-request timing to better mirror real traffic?

If we can get answers to those and the dry-run looks good, procurement and PO will be ready to sign by calendar week 3.

Thanks — Priya
